audits.title: 286 Two-Cycle Audit on Post-Tonsillectomy Analgesia
audits.standard: National standards; new ibuprofen guidance 7.5mg/kg QDS
audits.setting: Bristol Royal Hospital for Children; children undergoing tonsillectomy

cycle1.result: 95% prescribed inadequate ibuprofen (mean 5.5mg/kg); 6% presented with bleeding, none returned to theatre.

audits.intervention: New ibuprofen prescribing guideline (7.5mg/kg QDS instead of 5mg/kg TDS) with reduced opioid prescribing.

cycle2.result: 55% prescribed correct 7.5mg/kg QDS; no readmissions for pain; low number of bleeds.

audits.other_findings: All readmissions for pain or haemorrhage in cycle 1 were on TDS ibuprofen; about 110 tonsillectomies per cycle (approximate).
audits.citation: Thamer M, Soltan I, Ojha S, Sinclair T, Saunders M, Gaskin J. 286 Two-Cycle Audit on Post-Tonsillectomy Analgesia. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad258.094.

audits.title: 1208 Post-Tonsillectomy Re-Admissions – a Real Pain in the Mouth for Our Patients
audits.standard: National Prospective Tonsillectomy Audit and ENT UK Tonsillectomy Commissioning standards: overall readmission <15%, pain readmission <1%, return to theatre <1%
audits.setting: Adult and paediatric tonsillectomy patients, The Royal Wolverhampton NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Overall readmissions 15.5%, pain readmissions 1.4% (n=1), return to theatre 2.8%; documentation of analgesia instruction and discharge medication 83%.

audits.intervention: Departmental education and dissemination of post-operative verbal/written patient education.

cycle2.result: Overall readmissions 9.3%, pain readmissions 2.3% (n=1), return to theatre 0%; documentation of analgesia instruction and discharge medication 98%.

audits.other_findings: Length of stay compliant throughout (0.2, 0.1 days); pain readmission remained above standard; a pharmacist-led pain protocol and discharge analgesia pack are planned.
audits.citation: Al-Hity S, Rajdev K, Giblett N. 1208 Post-Tonsillectomy Re-Admissions – a Real Pain in the Mouth for Our Patients. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad258.353.

audits.title: Implementing a standardised discharge analgesia guideline to reduce paediatric post tonsillectomy pain.
audits.setting: Otolaryngology department, Musgrove Park Hospital, Taunton (district general hospital)

cycle1.result: 25 (16.6%) readmitted; 13 (8.6%) readmitted for pain control; 12 (7.9%) postoperative haemorrhage; discharge analgesia varied widely.

audits.intervention: Standardised weight-based algorithm for regular paracetamol for 2 weeks (standardised discharge analgesia protocol).

cycle2.result: 17 (14.4%) readmitted; 0 readmitted for pain control (reduction from 7.3% to 0%, p = 0.0027); 12 (10.2%) postoperative haemorrhage.

audits.other_findings: No significant change in overall readmission rate or haemorrhage rate (8.9% overall); over-the-counter analgesia was dosed by age rather than weight.
audits.citation: Shelton FR, Ishii H, Mella S, Chew D, Winterbottom J, Walijee H, et al.. Implementing a standardised discharge analgesia guideline to reduce paediatric post tonsillectomy pain. Int J Pediatr Otorhinolaryngol. 2018;111:54-58. doi:10.1016/j.ijporl.2018.05.020. PMID: 29958614.

audits.title: Paediatric Day Case Tonsillectomy - Audit of a New Programme.
audits.standard: ENT UK and Royal College of Surgeons maximum acceptable unplanned admission/readmission rate of 15%
audits.setting: Children's Health Ireland at Temple Street, Dublin (new paediatric day case programme)

cycle1.result: 6/34 (17.6%) admitted from day ward or readmitted within 30 days (95% CI 4.8%-30.5%, p = 0.33, not significantly above 15%).

audits.other_findings: Four readmissions (11.8%) were for bleeding, one for nausea and poor intake, one for sleep apnoea concerns; anaesthetic techniques varied considerably.
audits.citation: Grant O, Harper P. Paediatric Day Case Tonsillectomy - Audit of a New Programme. Ir Med J. 2020;113(4):56. PMID: 32268049.

audits.title: Decreasing Seven-Day Revisits After Pediatric Tonsillectomy: A Multidisciplinary and Comprehensive Unit-Based Safety Program (CUSP)-Driven Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.standard: Vizient national top-quartile benchmark seven-day revisit rate 2.17%; aim to reduce revisit rate by at least 1% by December 31, 2025
audits.setting: WVU Medicine Golisano Children's Hospital, tertiary children's hospital, Morgantown, West Virginia

cycle1.result: Seven-day revisit rate 3.75% (39/1041); pain and dehydration main drivers.

audits.intervention: Perioperative bundle: intraoperative crystalloid >=30 ml/kg, acetaminophen and dexamethasone; scheduled PACU ibuprofen; tolerance-based hydration readiness; standardised discharge packet with hydration checklist and dye-free medication calendar; surgical team PACU check-ins (three PDSA cycles).

cycle2.result: Seven-day revisit rate 2.16% (n = 15); by cycle: PDSA 1 2.83% (7/247), PDSA 2 1.65% (7/423), PDSA 3 0.75% (1/133).

audits.other_findings: Pain remained the main reason for revisit after the interventions; no formal statistical analysis.
audits.citation: Deskins C, Dabbous H, Smith S, Hankey B, Rickenbach O, Jones WS, et al.. Decreasing Seven-Day Revisits After Pediatric Tonsillectomy: A Multidisciplinary and Comprehensive Unit-Based Safety Program (CUSP)-Driven Quality Improvement Initiative. Cureus. 2025;17(12):e100068. doi:10.7759/cureus.100068. PMID: 41458343.
